"In a business setting, ego can lead to possessiveness, erratic decision-making, and a toxic work environment."

"If you can’t balance — or better yet, embrace — your ego, you won’t be able to make rational, intuitive decisions."
""
"You’ll insert too much of yourself into a situation and base any decisions off of how it may affect you personally."
""
"To evolve past this protectionist tribal mindset and focus on a more collaborative style of business and leadership, you'll have to learn to unlearn! "
""
"So, here’s how to grow past ego and become a better leader in the process:"
""
"1️⃣ Practice Radical Presence: If you listen to people, rather than inserting yourself into their situation, they’ll tell you what they want. Truly listening builds trust and connection with other people."
""
"2️⃣ Release Attachment to Ideas: No one owns an idea. The concept of “my idea” is pure ego. Business leaders without ego act as conduits and channels for a vision. They don’t take credit or try to own the idea, they just catalyze bring it to fruition."
""
"3️⃣ Develop Self-Awareness: If you feel like your ego might be in the driver’s seat in certain scenarios, then you need to begin soliciting feedback and truly listening to it. By consistently giving and receiving feedback, you can start challenging yourself to truly be present and hear what other people are telling you."
""
"4️⃣ Prioritize Self-Care: It may seem counterintuitive to focus on yourself when trying to eliminate your ego. But the reality is that you need to feel fulfilled and satisfied with who you are before you can begin leading others without thinking about yourself. To do that, you have to set boundaries and be firm about your own needs."
""
"When you rely on your ego to make decisions, they won’t be in the best interest of the team. But when you grow past ego, you can look at the situation with clear eyes and make the best decision for everyone involved."
